request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have a to-date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works now:**
- **Which rate applies:** the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date is chosen, as before. If that rate's to-date has passed, the claim's due is n/a. It doesn't fall back to an older rate, which matches the test (a claim dated after a closed rate shows n/a even though an always-on rate exists).
- **What follows from n/a:** totals and rollups skip the claim, a statement binds n/a, and there's no late charge. These needed no extra code because they already handle "no rate". The "in force today" figure also shows n/a once today's rate has ended.
- **Refusing bad dates:** a to-date before the from-date is refused on the server (a 400 error), in the database (a check constraint), and in the form, which shows `rate-form-error` without sending anything. A to-date with a blank from-date is allowed.
- **Audit:** `RATE_SET` adds ` to=<date>` at the end of the line only when a to-date was given.

**What changed:**
- **Database:** new migration `V32__rate_to_date.sql` adds a nullable `to_date` column to `rate`.
- **Server:**
  - `Rate.java` gets the `toDate` field and an `appliesOn(date)` check.
  - Both rate lookups (`RateService.rateOn` and `RollupService.rateOn`) now drop a rate whose to-date has passed.
  - `RateService.set` takes the to-date and refuses one before the from-date with the new `RateDatesException`.
  - `RateController` accepts and returns `to`.
- **Front end:** in `rates.ts`, `rateOn` follows the same rule. The form has a new `rate-form-to` field, and the rates table has a "To" column (`rate-to`) that shows "no end" when a rate has none.

Setting a rate again for the same grade and from-date also replaces its to-date; leaving the field blank clears it.
